💡 Key Takeaways
  • The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.
  • The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.
  • Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, customers will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is crucial to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, stablecoin giant Tether [USDT] has been making some moves lately. Here’s the rundown.

Tether has backed Argentine fintech app Lemon, with the former not putting a number on it when it unveiled the deal. Lemon did, however, saying that the package is worth $14.5 million.

According to recent reports, according to Lemon CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli, only $5 million of that is an actual investment in the company’s shares. The other $9.5 million is an incentive proposal linked to products the two will build together.

Industry observers note that there’s a lot that’s unclear right now though. Neither side has shared Lemon’s valuation or how big a stake Tether is getting. There’s also no word on how or when the $9.5 million gets paid out. Tether is after more consumers for USDT and Tether Gold [XAUT] across Latin America. Lemon gives it a decent shot at that. The app is said to have 4.5 million verified users, and its main balance runs on USDT.

Worth noting, however, that Lemon’s not the only home for Tether this month.

On the 9th, D3 rolled out a USD vault for Tether’s stablecoin. Customers can deposit USDT, keep an eye on their position, and withdraw without leaving the platform.

According to recent reports, sentora built the system using its Earn OS and Upshift tools, which decide where deposited funds go. Money moves with the market, within a set of risk rules. It is noted that the setup has already handled more than $2 billion.

Sources indicate that domain buyers usually come in, make a deal, and leave. Earning on stablecoins gives them a reason to keep their money on the platform.

Just don’t mistake automated for guaranteed. Returns depend on the lending markets the vault uses. So, consumers are still trusting a whole stack of infrastructure with their dollars.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried would consider a return to crypto and philanthropy after his time in prison, while weighing the impact on his reputation.
  • In an interview with Eli Goldfine, SBF discussed possible options after his release amid the negative impact on his reputation.
  • Sources indicate that SBF remarked he would consider it depending on when and how he got out, and he also commented on the criminal justice system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried would consider a return to crypto and philanthropy after his time in prison, while weighing the impact on his reputation. The embattled digital asset executive was sentenced after an infamous collapse that plunged the sector into murky waters.

In an interview with Eli Goldfine, SBF discussed possible options after his release amid the negative impact on his reputation. He might make a crypto return despite this past run with the collapsed crypto exchange, FTX.

Sources indicate that SBF remarked he would consider it depending on when and how he got out, and he also commented on the criminal justice system. His return to finance and crypto is to resume earning money for charitable donations and other causes.

“I would strongly consider it. It would depend on when I got out and how. I’d strongly consider crypto, AI, and finance more generally… “I think Anthropic is clearly one of, if not the top, AI companies,” he stated.

It has been revealed that previously, SBF was substantial on donations through the concept of earning to give, urging wealthy founders to direct a portion of their earnings to charity. Though in jail, SBF is keen on artificial intelligence and its impact on finance and technology.

Recent findings suggest that per the interview, he tipped small companies built around AI products scaling between $100 million and $1 billion within years. This follows the ongoing AI wave attracting billions from traditional investors, underscoring capital rotation from other sectors.

Anthropic’s IPO has led to funds circling the market, with whales targeting upcoming highs in related stocks. Meanwhile, crypto products have suffered, with asset prices falling to multi-month lows.

Furthermore, SBF warned against companies positioning as pro-AI just to attract funding. Recall that SBF backed Anthropic through Alameda Research, investing $500 million before selling its entire holdings in 2024 to pay debts.

While he planned his return after his sentence, SBF admitted his role in public discourse might be limited because of his current reputation. “…looking at public discourse, politics, and media, I’m not sure what role I could play, if any. But earning to give is a default.”.

Sources indicate that FTX collapsed in 2022, fueling a massive selloff and billions in losses. The aftermath led to tighter regulations and a lengthy investigation of executives linked to the exchange.

Breaking: XRP Ledger Lending System Nears Key Deployment Milestone

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (322 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Coinpedia

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SingleAssetVault activation is projected for December 9, subject to continued validator support.
  • XRPL stablecoin supply reached $836.90 million, with RLUSD representing 89.35%.
  • The proposed lending system supports uncollateralised loans, while borrower underwriting remains offchain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SingleAssetVault activation is projected for December 9, subject to continued validator support.

XRPL stablecoin supply reached $836.90 million, with RLUSD representing 89.35%.

The proposed lending system supports uncollateralised loans, while borrower underwriting remains offchain.

The XRP Ledger lending system is getting closer to deployment, but don’t confuse a countdown with a working loan market. The SingleAssetVault amendment is projected to activate on December 9, provided validator support holds. The separate LendingProtocol amendment still needs approval.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, XRPL stablecoin supply has reached $836.90 million. RLUSD accounts for 89.35% of that total, according to November 27 figures. That’s a sizeable balance, but it isn’t money already committed to lending.

The SingleAssetVault amendment would establish infrastructure for pooling a single asset and issuing depositors shares representing their interest. The LendingProtocol amendment performs a different job: it enables brokers to arrange fixed-term loans and record repayments on the ledger.

XRPL amendments need more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks. If support falls short, the waiting period can restart. So December 9 remains a projection, not a guaranteed launch date.

The proposed system supports uncollateralised loans, making borrower assessment a serious glitch for depositors. Underwriting and risk management happen offchain, according to the lending specification.

Sources indicate that brokers may also contribute optional first-loss capital in the same asset as the loan pool. That can absorb some missed-payment losses, but it isn’t a blanket guarantee.

The XRP Ledger Foundation has published an open-source reference application demonstrating the system on Devnet. It combines vaults and lending with credentials, permissioned domains and batch transactions.

In a recent development, still, a working demonstration isn’t commercial adoption. XRPL DeFi total value locked stands at about $30.65 million, a separate measure from the $836.94 million stablecoin balance.

The XRP Ledger lending system now needs amendment activation, production markets and funded loans before stablecoin supply can translate into actual lending activity.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) printed its first bullish RSI signal on the daily chart since September after rebounding from its lowest price since 2021. According to TradingView, SHIB's market cap was back above $2.1 billion on Friday and stood at $2.19 billion, about $500 million below its moving average at $2.67 billion ahead of Christmas.

SHIB was trading at around $0.0000037 on Friday, up 1.8% over 24 hours, according to TradingView. The token ranked No. 34 on the platform with a market cap of $2.18 billion.

Recent findings suggest that the relative strength index (RSI) on the chart fell below 30 on Nov. 14, which is usually considered an oversold reading. The indicator stayed under that level until this week and reached 35 on Friday.

Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

In a single proposal executed on 4 November, API3 permanently capped supply, ended emissions, moved to one-token-one-vote governance, and removed its own ability to mint tokens, while pointing its signed-data infrastructure at the fast-growing economy of AI agents.

Industry observers note that API3, a provider of first-party data infrastructure, has executed a proposal that resets the protocol on three fronts at once: its token, its governance, and its mission. The proposal permanently capped API3’s supply at 200,000,000, ended five years of token emissions, moved governance to a simpler one-token-one-vote model, and removed the protocol’s ability to ever mint fresh tokens. Together, the changes clear the ground for a sharper focus on bringing signed, verifiable data to decentralized finance and to AI agents.

Since 2021, API3’s staking pool has minted about 90.1 million tokens, roughly 47% of today’s supply, at a pace near 950,000 a week, or close to 26% a year. The proposal minted API3 one final time to reach exactly 200,000,000, removed every minter, and transferred ownership of the token contract to a dead address that no one controls. No newly introduced API3 can ever be created, and the token’s maximum supply, listed until then as effectively unlimited, is fixed and final.

SIMPLER GOVERNANCE, A SMALLER ATTACK SURFACE.

Governance moves from the framework API3 built in 2021 to a streamlined model on Snapshot. Each API3 token counts as one vote, whether it is staked or simply held, and the DAO’s multisignature wallets execute what passes. Retiring the old contracts and ending the token’s mintability also closes a specific risk: a hostile vote reaching the mintable token contract and printing latest supply.

Industry observers note that hostile votes have drained treasuries across DeFi, and an unlimited mint was the bigger prize. With no minter to capture and no owner to compromise, that path is removed. The change comes as the cost of finding smart-contract exploits falls sharply, making old, rarely touched code a standing target.

It has been revealed that with its foundations settled, API3 is concentrating on where its five years of API and DeFi experience applies next. Its curation business runs on-chain lending markets on the price feeds it builds across Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain, backing them with its own treasury capital alongside outside depositors, a structure it calls skin in the game.

It has been revealed that airnodeHub, now live in early access at airnodehub.api3.org, extends API3’s provider-signed model to the wider API market, letting AI agents discover, verify, and pay original providers for signed data. As agents become a growing share of internet traffic and begin paying for data per call, API3 is positioning AirnodeHub as the place that work is sourced and paid for.

A DEFLATIONARY DESIGN FUNDED BY REVENUE.

Revenue from API3’s live operations, its curation business and the activity behind it, already buys API3 on the open market every month. AirnodeHub does not yet earn revenue; once per-request payments go live, it is designed to add to those buybacks as well. With emissions ended and supply fixed, the token is built to be deflationary over time: a capped asset with recurring, revenue-funded buy-side demand in place of a steady flow of newly minted tokens.

API3 builds data infrastructure that delivers signed, real-world data directly from the providers that produce it. It runs first-party data feeds across DeFi, curates on-chain lending markets on those feeds, and is extending its provider-signed model to the wider API market through AirnodeHub. API3 is governed by its token holders through the API3 DAO, with a fixed supply of 200,000,000. The project’s broader work and the marketplace itself can be explored at api3.org and airnodehub.api3.org.

The Commission just granted a multi-faceted sanction package going ham on Russia’s various uses of crypto.

The European Commission’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia extends the European Union’s (EU) transaction ban to over 60 Russian banks and says all 60 of those will be removed from SWIFT, President Ursula von der Leyen said in Strasbourg on 23 November 2026.

Industry observers note that this comes just weeks after Russia officially legalized crypto currency trading, starting with the substantial-cap coins like Bitcoin (BTC) & Ethereum (ETH). In the 22nd sanction packet, Russian-linked crypto services & platforms were specifically named as banned for transactions.

According to recent reports, “The measures include the possibility for EU firms to sue their non-Russian contractual parties in the EU to recover damages.”, – states the document. “We will continue to propose new sanctions until Russia highlights genuine intent for a lasting peace in Ukraine”, further mentioned the Chief Commissioner.

Industry observers note that with this package, we are increasing the pressure.We are striking harder at Russia’s ways to finance its war, by targeting its banks and crypto platforms.We are further isolating Russia. We are shutting the door to its participation to European sports and cultural events.… pic.twitter.com/9Ltkpohylq.

While focusing on Russian SWIFT sanctions, the EU added 51 entities to the anti-circumvention list, while the majority of them, 27, were outside Russia: 14 came from China, including four in Hong Kong, four in Türkiye, three in Kyrgyzstan, two in India, two in Kazakhstan and two more in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

Sources indicate that the European Union (EU) freshly assembled the Crypto Task Force to counter upcoming crypto-related ways of evading the huge pile of sanctions, including limitations of Russian business abroad via ‘third-world’ parties. The Council will decide when the ban enters into force, after the necessary measures are activated.

Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

According to recent reports, in a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, remarked it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

Sources indicate that the development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

In a recent development, the Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

Industry observers note that as of the latest update by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are currently being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Upgrade Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Upgrade Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Update Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it.
  • In a recent development, this vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum.
  • Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it. This, using a payment worth less than $0.35. For context, each planted transaction costs just $0.18 to $0.34, depending on the address format.

In a recent development, this vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

This is the reason why this revelation has raised an vital question about Bitcoin’s privacy — Can someone identify the IP address associated with a Bitcoin wallet, even if the wallet owner never publicly reveals their identity?

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

In a recent development, to understand the vulnerability, it is important to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many owners operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

Recent findings suggest that according to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node unveils the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

Recent findings suggest that on the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Therefore, even watch-only wallets, which monitor addresses without holding their private keys, can be affected. This also means that avoiding address reuse alone may not be enough to protect wallet privacy.

According to recent reports, hence, as a potential workaround, customers can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the matter, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

The wild SWIFT replacement claim resurfaces on social media for a good reason: XRP-tied banks are in.

According to recent reports, two recent posts have put long-term XRP price projections back in view. One centers on a multi-year chart pattern with an $8.30 target, while the other argues that full replacement of SWIFT would support valuations above $15,000. XRP is trading near $0.95.

Analyst EGRAG CRYPTO highlighted a weekly chart showing a large symmetrical triangle that XRP broke out of in prior years. The X post stated that the original white triangle’s measured breakout target of $8.30 has not yet been reached and suggested the current price action could represent a macro retest of that breakout before any larger expansion.

#XRP – The $8.30 Number 🎯:This remains one of my most powerful macro charts.The original white symmetrical triangle breakout target has STILL not been reached.What if everything happening right now is simply the macro retest of that breakout before the real expansion?My… pic.twitter.com/F0tdM5mxtl.

Industry observers note that A separate post by Ripple_Mino claimed that if XRP fully replaces SWIFT, the token could be valued beyond $15,000. The argument rests on XRP’s divisibility: one XRP equals one million drops, so even extreme valuations would still allow practical fractional use.

Official and recent developments do not support the premise of XRP’s SWIFT replacement.

SWIFT has released its own blockchain-based shared ledger for tokenized bank deposits, with more than a dozen major banks participating in trials. SWIFT has not announced any integration of XRP as a settlement asset for that system.

Former SWIFT innovation leadership has publicly rejected claims of XRP integration, and the network continues to emphasize its own infrastructure and tokenized deposits rather than a single external token.

The $8.30 figure is a technical target drawn from a multi-year chart structure, while the $15,000 figure is a hypothetical based on a scenario that SWIFT and major participating banks haven’t endorsed yet.

It has been revealed that neither projection is reflected in current market pricing yet or officially top-confirmed institutional commitments. XRP’s price action continues to trade well below both levels as of late November 2026.

The link between SWIFT as a traditional financial intermediary and XRP’s native chain comes multi-layered, with intersection across liquidity provision and instant settlement environments.

In a recent development, bitcoin shorts lost $64.9 million over 24 hours, and Bitcoin longs lost $20.9 million, according to CoinGlass. Sources indicate that ethereum shorts lost $38.1 million, the second-largest amount among all assets on CoinGlass. ETH traded at around $1,721 on Friday, up 1% over 24 hours.

Sources indicate that according to CoinGlass, Solana gained 3.3% to around $73, and SOL shorts lost $6 million. XRP rose 1.9% to $0.97, and its shorts lost $2 million.

Industry observers note that deribit's monthly Bitcoin options expiry took place at 08:00 UTC on Friday. About 110,800 BTC contracts, worth roughly $6.75 billion, expired with a max pain price of $70,000, according to Deribit data.

BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes warned about the weekend in an X post on Friday. "If there is no Fed dovish rhetoric pivot before the pre-FOMC blackout begins EOD Fri US time, this weekend could get spicy," Hayes wrote. He added that liquid assets and crypto could get dumped before Monday's open.

According to recent reports, earlier this week, Hayes remarked that Bitcoin "will retest $55k" and shared a chart with the price at $58,773. On Nov. 21, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150, its lowest price since September 2024.

It has been revealed that at its October meeting, the Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10–2 vote. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a quarter-point hike.

It has been revealed that the Fed's blackout period starts at midnight ET on Nov. 28, and the FOMC will announce its rate decision on Dec. 9. CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at 100% on Nov. 12.

In a recent development, conConAI’s $CON token is attracting market attention following its November 6, 2026 launch on Uniswap v4. In a CoinMarketCap snapshot retrieved November 26, $CON traded at approximately $0.06582, up more than 619% from its recorded launch-day low of $0.009144. The token has also moved above its planned $0.01 launch reference price, while ConConAI continues developing its AI advisor network and partner listings system.

The performance follows a sold-out presale on November 4 and a public market debut two days later. According to ConConAI’s launch upgrade, $CON reached the number-one top-gainer position on CoinMarketCap during its first 24 hours of trading. With the presale completed, the token has entered a latest stage of market exposure, allowing a wider audience of traders, investors, and crypto publications to assess its performance and the project behind it.

Industry observers note that A lot has changed since the token’s first days on the market. ConConAI now reports more than 1,800 holders, a completed audit of the live $CON contract, a completed first monthly burn, and expanded development capacity. The project says its next phase will focus on building the listings system, advisors, and token-payment functionality in parallel.

Sources indicate that coinMarketCap recorded $CON’s launch-period low at approximately $0.009144 on November 6. The token subsequently reached an all-time high of approximately $0.08434 on November 24. In the November 26 snapshot, it was trading at approximately $0.06582, representing an increase of about 619.9% from its recorded low.

The movement has not been a continuous upward trend. After its initial market debut, $CON experienced price fluctuations before reaching a new all-time high later in November. Such volatility can occur during the early trading period of a newly launched cryptocurrency, as buyers and sellers establish a market price. The token’s current distance from its latest high is therefore worth monitoring alongside its longer-term performance.

The November 26 CoinMarketCap snapshot showed a market capitalisation of approximately $3.01 million and 24-hour trading volume of about $155,650. It also reported approximately 2,180 holders. These figures provide a more recent view of market participation than the November 12 snapshot.

The token’s performance occurred during a difficult month for the broader crypto market. ConConAI says $CON’s movement has been driven by its own fundamentals, including a live product, transparent token information, and continued development. That explanation reflects the project’s position; price movement alone cannot establish what caused buying interest, and the broader market can still affect $CON.

Several developments give $CON a potentially constructive outlook as it moves beyond its initial listing period.

Sources indicate that first, the token has established market visibility through its CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko listings, its reported first-day top-gainer position, and its early trading performance. Continued visibility could bring additional market participants to the project, although listings and past gains do not guarantee future demand.

Second, ConConAI has reported that 40.15 million tokens have been burned from the original 100 million supply, leaving an effective supply of 59.85 million $CON. The first two burns removed 20 million tokens each, followed by a monthly burn of 150,000 $CON on November 19. The project says further 150,000-token burns are scheduled monthly, with the next one planned for December 15. Future burns remain scheduled events until completed and verified on-chain.

It has been revealed that third, the token has a planned utility within ConConAI’s commercial network. If the platform attracts consumers and businesses, the intended use of $CON for partner listings, placements, and performance-based fees could create a more substantial demand story than trading interest alone. The development tracker presently places the first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

The combination of early market strength, reduced token supply, and an evolving utility model gives market participants several reasons to consider buying $CON.

ConConAI’s broader proposition is built around bringing back the personal purchase advisor, powered by artificial intelligence. Instead of navigating endless search results and comparing countless products, customers describe what they need. A specialist AI advisor asks relevant questions, interprets the requirements, and returns one recommendation with the reason behind it.

Recent findings suggest that the consumer remains in control. The AI does not make purchases on the user’s behalf, and the final decision always belongs to the user.

Seven specialist advisors are live, covering categories that include investment guidance, travel, cars, film, health information, music, and real estate. The project’s aim is to make AI useful in everyday purchasing decisions by helping people move from describing a need to identifying a relevant option.

It has been revealed that businesses can also submit products and services to the network. ConConAI’s stated model is that payment does not buy recommendation rank: a listing is intended to appear only when it honestly matches what the user asked for, with fit taking priority. This approach is designed to connect consumers with suitable offers while giving participating businesses another way to reach potential customers.

Until an exchange makes its own announcement or an agreement is confirmed, the plans remain subject to change.

The project says pool fees currently help cover development and marketing costs, with partner payments expected to contribute once the listings platform opens.

These are useful verification and discovery signals, but they do not eliminate market, smart-contract or third-party platform risks.

Its published allocation includes 30 million $CON for the community, 15 million for liquidity, 10 million for centralized-exchange liquidity, and approximately 5 million for project purposes. The project says its allocation wallets use Safe multisig arrangements. The official contract address is 0x7ad1A8Fc42Ac150B04dED5825D21a0C90b6d28D8.

Recent findings suggest that if the project converts its existing development progress into wider consumer adoption and partner participation, the token’s intended utility could become an increasingly vital part of its market proposition. Combined with the reported supply reduction and community-led roadmap, these factors provide a positive basis for watching $CON’s next phase, while recognising the volatility and risks associated with newly rolled out crypto assets.

  • Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a newly introduced initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets.

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a newly introduced initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

As cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s new VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

In a recent development, the initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

The exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular people and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, stated, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our consumers engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”.

It has been revealed that both upcoming and existing Binance users can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, customers can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

Industry observers note that the program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance users.

According to recent reports, the additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Users who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?

According to recent reports, kuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November. Deposits have already been closed permanently too.

Industry observers note that withdrawals will close at 08:00 UTC on 31st December 2026. KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier over project-related concerns, with the exchange also warning that stablecoin conversion of remaining balances won’t be guaranteed.

Industry observers note that at press time, CoinGecko highlighted $90.42 million in combined 24-hour volumes across KuCoin’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs. Together, they accounted for 50.27% of Monero’s spot trading volume.

Including XMR/BTC and XMR/ETH, that brought KuCoin’s total to $104.60 million or 58.14%.

Hence, the question: Where could that trading move now? At the time of writing, the remaining exchanges demonstrated more buy orders close to the market price, despite reporting a lower turnover.

Recent findings suggest that kraken’s XMR/USD pair had approximately $386,970 in buy orders within 2% below its price, compared to KuCoin’s XMR/USDT pair’s $85,683. WhiteBIT and HTX’s XMR/USDT pairs highlighted $260,810 and $196,231, respectively.

It has been revealed that that gave Kraken roughly 4.5 times KuCoin’s nearby buying depth, with WhiteBIT and HTX also offering larger buy-side cushions. These orders could help absorb selling, although traders could cancel them at any time.

That access problem extended into services marketed as alternatives to CEXs.

X user and the founder of XMRHub called KuCoin’s delisting “the most bearish thing for $XMR.” According to the exec, the exchange supported swap services, liquidity, and onboarding.

Recent findings suggest that dash’s Joel Valenzuela also raised a similar concern. He warned that further CEX losses could make no-KYC Monero swaps harder to obtain.

Finally, Cake Wallet founder Vik Sharma also directed customers towards wallet-based swaps, writing,.

Recent findings suggest that why does Monero keep getting delisted? Because it works!

It has been revealed that the announcement followed another loss of exchange access earlier that month. MEXC ended XMR spot trading on 17th November. Its XMR Perpetual Futures closed separately on 13th November.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold has reached its highest level on record, according to Galaxy Research data. The measure peaked at 0.56 on Oct. 22 and broke the previous record of 0.50, which Galaxy dated to Nov. 6, 2020.

Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy Digital, posted about the record on X on Friday. "Bitcoin isn't digital gold? Bitcoin reaches highest correlation to gold of all time," he wrote.

Thorn shared two Galaxy Research charts together with the post. According to the charts, the 90-day correlation was at 0.54 on Nov. 23, and the 30-day correlation stood at 0.59 on the same day.

In a recent development, in the first half of 2026, the 90-day correlation stayed near 0.1. It started to rise in July and climbed above 0.50 by early October, according to Galaxy's data. Between 2020 and 2025, the average reading was 0.11.

On Jan. 20, Galaxy CEO Mike Novogratz wrote on X that "the gold price is telling us we are losing reserve currency status at an accelerating rate." "$BTC is disappointing as it is still being met with selling," he added.

It has been revealed that thorn wrote about Bitcoin and gold on X in February. "Bitcoin's failure to trade like gold as part of 'the debasement trade' since Sep. '25 damaged its narrative with new entrants," he wrote. "When bitcoiners said 'digital gold,' they were describing its fundamental properties, not that it's high beta to gold today," he added.

According to recent reports, on Wednesday, Galaxy published a report that withdrew its Oct. 26 call on the Bitcoin bear market. "We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June," the report noted. Thorn shared it on X with the comment, "As it turns out, the Bitcoin bear market is definitely not over.".

According to the report, Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 22 at $61,104 after seven straight weekly losses. Thorn wrote in the report that the level to watch was $58,525, Bitcoin's closing low from June 30. According to Thorn, a daily close below that level would mark "the start of a move to a materially lower low.".

"The clock claims this bear is overdue to end; the depth says it has further to fall," the report mentioned. On Nov. 22, the bear market was 412 days old, and earlier ones lasted 163 to 406 days from high to low, according to Galaxy.

Bitcoin was down 53% from its October 2025 record at that point. In past bear markets, it lost 77% to 93%. If the June low breaks, Galaxy sees possible latest lows at about $48,500 and $28,200.

Galaxy tracks 13 bottom signals, and two of them have been met so far. According to the report, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs held about 1.24 million BTC, down 71,339 BTC since Oct. 4.

On Nov. 17, SkyBridge Capital founder Anthony Scaramucci asked Novogratz at the Digital Assets Forum in New York whether Bitcoin could return to $90,000 by the end of 2026. "Unlikely now," Novogratz said. "Less likely than it was. You need something to happen," he added.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.
  • Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.
  • Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin whales have defied the negative trend seen in the Q4s of the past nine years as they have accumulated billions of dollars' worth of Bitcoin since Q4 2026 began.

Even though Bitcoin has faced severe price corrections during the period, with its price retesting levels not seen this year, Bitcoin whales have continued to buy the asset.

Onchain data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that Bitcoin wallet addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC have increased their holdings by 121,117 BTC in Q4 2026.

This defies the trend seen in the last nine Q4s, as Bitcoin whales have historically reduced their holdings during Q4 of each of the last nine years.

The source shared historic data from 2017, revealing that the Bitcoin whales recorded balance declines in seven of the last nine Q4 periods, with only 2019 and 2020 recording increases.

This means that the increase seen this month marks a major reversal of that historical trend, especially as Bitcoin has suffered even bigger price losses this Q4, dropping by about 29.5% over the same 52-day period.

Following the increase in Bitcoin whale accumulation seen in this quarter, further data shows that the whales now hold about 2.947 million BTC as of November 21, 2026.

Despite the increase in the holdings of Bitcoin whales this Q4, data also demonstrated that these large holders have seen their unrealized profits drop significantly.

As such, unrealized profits among addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have fallen to about $23.8 billion. Notably, this represents a massive decrease from the $124.7 billion recorded on September 30 and the record $294.4 billion in gains achieved on August 14, 2025.

#168902. A Minimalist House in Italy Makes the Case for Less

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (760 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Architecturaldigest ↗ Open Full Page

A Minimalist House in Italy Makes the Case for Less

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (760 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the friendship between John Pawson and Noona Smith-Petersen began in New York City in a very 1990s way: working for Calvin Klein.
  • Pawson had already earned a reputation for restraint.
  • Furnished with Hans Wegner chairs and a Pawson-designed table, the dining area opens onto the land thanks to a sliding window wall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the friendship between John Pawson and Noona Smith-Petersen began in New York City in a very 1990s way: working for Calvin Klein. Pawson, then an architectural wunderkind from the United Kingdom, and Smith-Petersen, a young Danish-Italian communications manager for the fashion house, found themselves collaborating on the opening of the brand’s first flagship on Madison Avenue.

Pawson had already earned a reputation for restraint. His earliest residential works (a Mallorca summer house for collectors, an art dealer’s London apartment) provided a series of simple surfaces, plinths, and frames—for objects, for vistas, and for life. The same was true at the Calvin Klein store, where designer and client amplified each other’s design approaches in a meeting of minimalist minds.

Furnished with Hans Wegner chairs and a Pawson-designed table, the dining area opens onto the land thanks to a sliding window wall.

The living area features a table and chairs by Poul Kjærholm.

A sauna is clad in blackened wood.

It has been revealed that pawson’s recent residence for Smith-Petersen and her husband, Enrico Erba Springorum, an Armani executive, makes another case for life with less. “The imprint came from childhood: the minimalism, the Danish design,” explains Smith-Petersen, who grew up outside Copenhagen. “Poul Kjærholm was our neighbor,” she adds, name-checking the widely influential midcentury modernist. There were also formative summers spent at the pared-back house her father designed on the Turkish peninsula of Çeşme. About the location, she recalls, “People remarked, ‘You guys are crazy!’ But it was a place close to nature and the sea. And then later it became a destination.”.

A single sculptural tree dots the courtyard.

An oak bed with integrated bedside tables anchors the primary bedroom.

Ninety minutes south of Milan, the patchwork hills of the Val Luretta are far less isolated. Its proximity to the city has attracted editors, artists, and other creatives in search of space and quiet. That tranquility drew Smith-Petersen to the area when she was seeking land on which to build a compound with her younger brother, Henrik, for their families. (She and her husband have two adult sons.) Over the years, she and Pawson had maintained a friendship. “So when Henrik and I found the property, I had this crazy idea: Why don’t I ask John?” claims Smith-Petersen. “My brother said, ‘Forget it!’ But we went to visit John and his team in London and it kicked off from there.”.

The primary bath’s bespoke vanity, topped in a Grassi Pietri surface.

Smith-Petersen stands in the living area.

A view across the dining table toward the minimalist hearth.

Sources indicate that the resulting structure, realized with project architect Giulio Marchesi, is the irst of two planned homes on the site, one for each sibling. Sitting long and low on the land, like an ivory piano key dropped onto the hillside, the single-story house frames expansive views of the Val Luretta. “The area of the countryside is so dramatic,” reflects Pawson, whose first visit to the site was in winter fog. “In the summer, it’s very different—it’s so lush.”.

At some 2,500 square feet, the house is spacious but intimate, with Pawson’s trademark spareness and remarkable warmth. He designed it along one axis, a long corridor connecting the foyer to the open-plan kitchen, dining area, and living area, then bedrooms beyond. White-painted plaster walls and floors of pale-gray stone, sourced nearby in Vicenza, radiate calm. As Pawson explains, understanding the way the body and the eye move through a space is paramount—and can take time. “You’ve got to learn the choreography,” he notes. Living in and feeling the house is key.

Smith-Petersen and Pawson on-site.

Industry observers note that the yearslong friendship Pawson and Smith-Petersen had forged helped him understand how she would use the space. There would be mornings at the Pawson-designed table, afternoons on the terrace or under one of the century-old oaks, and evenings making dinner in a kitchen brimming with Scandinavian tableware. In solitude or surrounded by family, there’s complete peace on offer.

The open-plan dining area and kitchen.

“Most architects—contemporaries, colleagues—always say, ‘Oh, it’s impossible, a private house,’ ” indicates Pawson. The process can be “very emotional. And that’s what makes it good.” Luckily for Smith-Petersen, the primary feeling the house evokes is serenity. “I didn’t expect to be in such awe,” she says. “I was never a country person. Sometimes, I try to arrive a day before anyone else is here and do a silent retreat,” she adds. “It’s where I feel best now. It’s pure joy.”.

Bitcoin Developer Warns Google Play Policy Could Lead to Home Invasions

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's blueprint to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.
  • For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.
  • "There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 27, Bitcoin developer Peter Todd warned that Google's blueprint to publicly display developers' addresses on the Play Store could lead to home invasions targeting developers of Bitcoin apps.

For independent developers working from home, the address displayed on Google Play could also be their residential address.

"There will be home invasions to compromise developers," Todd wrote on X.

He specifically highlighted the risks to developers of Bitcoin and other security-related apps, urging Google employees responsible for implementing the change to refuse to do so.

Starting March 1, 2027, Google Play will display the phone number and address of developers who use individual accounts to publish apps and identify themselves as traders.

Google explained that the requirement is related to its obligations as an online marketplace in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the UK.

The address and contact information will be visible to Play Store users worldwide.

The question is what address a developer might have to disclose, even for a relatively small app.

Dodemaide explained that Google support had informed him that he couldn't use a post office box because the address had to match his verified residential address.

He said he was considering removing his app from 31 countries to protect his home address.

Dodemaide also asked whether Google would allow individual developers to use a verified business mailing address instead.

Google lists several types of developers who may need to consider whether they qualify as traders, including those who sell apps, offer in-app purchases or earn advertising revenue.

For example, someone publishing an app purely as a hobby could declare themselves a non-trader.

Developers who don't distribute their apps in the EEA or UK are also considered non-traders under the policy.

Existing account holders have until Feb. 1, 2027, to submit their trader declarations, one month before the contact information becomes publicly visible.

Developers creating new accounts will need to make their declarations during account registration.

Google warns that failing to comply could prevent developers from updating their apps or result in their apps being removed from the Play Store globally.

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers.

The updated browser workspace adds an in-editor assistant as Solana expands its wider AI developer push.

Solana has rolled out a built-in AI coding agent inside Solana Playground, its browser-based development environment, aiming to help programmers learn, build, and deploy smart contracts without setting up local toolchains.

For traders and investors, it offers useful context on developer onboarding, Solana’s AI infrastructure push, and early-stage protocol risk.

In a post on X, Solana introduced the updated Solana Playground as a place to “learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser,” noting that the integrated agent explains existing code and edits it alongside the developer rather than writing full programs on its own.

Sources indicate that introducing Solana Playground – where you learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser. An AI agent explains the code and edits it with you. Start here: https://t.co/nM0ySqDkfO pic.twitter.com/SFKYYTx04n.

Builders can start projects using either Anchor, a framework that streamlines Solana program development, or native Solana programming, which offers lower-level control without framework abstractions.

In a recent development, according to product walk-throughs, the workspace includes three guided learning paths. These include an introductory Anchor tutorial called Hello Anchor and an intermediate build named Lumberjack. It also offers 10 sample Solana programs.

Browser-based Solana development predates the AI integration: the open-source Solana Playground (SolPg) has long let developers compile Rust programs, manage development wallets, and deploy contracts without a local CLI setup.

The latest release adds an in-editor assistant to explain unfamiliar code and apply edits within the same session.

The Playground patch fits into a wider push around AI and automated agents on Solana.

Solana’s developer portal now provides guidance for AI coding agents, while solana.ai focuses on autonomous trading, wallet management, and stablecoin payments.

The Solana Foundation has also introduced an open-source Confidential Compute toolkit with Nito for AI workloads involving sensitive data.

Figures shared by the Solana Foundation at Breakpoint 2026 indicated more than 120 teams are building AI products on Solana, with access to the Builder Program for grants, technical resources, hiring support, marketing help, and infrastructure credits.

Developer-focused releases rarely drive sustained moves in SOL or ecosystem tokens on their own. Liquidity, macro conditions, and net capital flows carry far more weight in the near term.

Industry observers note that however, lowering the barrier to write and iterate on code can speed up experimentation—and increase the volume of new or lightly tested contracts. Developer activity remains a key indicator of long-term ecosystem growth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Could the next 24 hours confirm Bitcoin’s bottom?

Bitcoin is down over 20% in November, marking its steepest monthly correction since June. Back then, BTC recovered from $55K to $85K over the next three months. A similar recovery now depends on reclaiming key resistance levels and flipping the market structure bullish. For starters though, BTC needs to establish a bottom.

At the time of writing, Glassnode data revealed that BTC was still defending its summer lows. August’s breakout above $80K has since fully retraced, bringing price back to June’s $60K support zone.

Sources indicate that although BTC briefly wicked below this level twice, every daily candle has closed above it. This could be a sign that buyers are defending this support level.

Meanwhile, other on-chain metrics are lending weight to the bottoming thesis.

In a recent development, bitcoin’s stablecoins have lost $21 billion in the last two months, mirroring what happened in 2022. Back then, a $33 billion reduction in stablecoin supply occurred ahead of BTC’s November low, suggesting that the current liquidity contraction could signal a similar market reset. On the flip-side though, reduced stablecoin liquidity reduces the funds that can be used to stimulate a market rally.

This puts the focus on the next 24 hours. Around $6.8 billion in Bitcoin Options are set to expire on Deribit at 08:00 UTC. With the put/call open interest ratio at 0.89 and heavy put positioning around $60K, the expiry could fuel further market volatility and test Bitcoin’s [BTC] bottoming structure.

Bitcoin’s latest Options expiry could prove critical.

On-chain data revealed that nearly $6.8 billion in Bitcoin Options will expire on Deribit, marking one of the month’s largest expiries. Max pain sat at around $70K-$73K, while BTC traded near $60.9K, leaving a gap of roughly 15%. Meanwhile, the put/call ratio climbed from 0.55 in October to 0.89. This suggested that traders have been becoming more defensive and adding protection against a potential Bitcoin price decline.

In a recent development, interestingly, the main bearish zones seemed to be at $60K, $58K, $50K and $40K. Significantly, $40K put options expire on Christmas Day. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETFs have continued to show net redemptions for seven days running. For the month of November alone, $5.39 billion has been redeemed, the highest ever monthly figure.

Consequently, the real test will now come after expiry.

Recent findings suggest that traders are placing more bets on Bitcoin’s price falling. At press time, put options were high at strike levels of $60K, $58K, $50K and $40K. However, maximum pain was indicated to be at significantly higher levels, showing a wide gap between current prices and Options positioning. Generally then, with the growing put/call ratio and elevated short interest, it would seem that traders may be bracing for further downside. They might not be anticipating a swift rebound either.

In short, Bitcoin is showing early signs of a potential bottom. However, shrinking stablecoin liquidity, record ETF outflows, and rising demand for downside protection allude to the presence of bearish pressure. The $6.8 billion Options expiry could add volatility, putting the critical $60K support to the test.

It has been revealed that picking up on the game quicker than you thought? You can skip the early stages and go for a complete set that allows you to learn how to optimize your shot-making skills. The Stix Perform Set is a complete 12-club set that will provide you with all the tools you need, all for under $1,000.

In a recent development, the Perform Set is the brand’s first set with the option for irons with a steel shaft, a boon for mid-high handicap players whose higher swing speeds may be a bit too much for the extra flex of graphite. Clubs that benefit from the flex (the driver, 3 wood, and 4 hybrid) still come standard with graphite, but having the choice when selecting irons is going to greatly increase the amount of time you’ll stick with your Stix.

It has been revealed that in my testing, I took the Stix out for a couple dozen rounds, walking and riding in a cart. The set is very manageable size-wise. The bag is light enough for comfortable wear but substantial enough to stay secure when strapped to the back of a golf cart. They’re some of the most forgiving clubs I've played and are well-built, resulting in improved distance and fewer mishits. My favorite club was the 4 iron hybrid—I've never hit a hybrid so well.

Another set from one of the most prestigious equipment brands in golf, the Cobra Fly XL set is the ideal set for someone who knows they’re going to be consistently hitting the golf course in a golf cart. The cart bag is big, sturdy, and spacious, while the wide range of clubs gives you options in every part of the course.

The Cobra brand is well-recognized, and these striking clubs will fit in with any other sets on the course, ensuring that your skills do the talking, not your equipment. If your skills are lacking, that’s okay, too, because each club in this set is super forgiving thanks to excellent weight distribution and optimized shape, from the driver right down through the putter.

According to recent reports, when you’re looking for a little more performance but still trying to stay affordable, PXG is a brand to look to. This Wildcat Bundle is an extremely versatile setup that utilizes premium materials and the same tech found in the brand’s standalone clubs, all tuned for maximum forgiveness and easy launch—must-haves for beginners.

While it is a hefty investment, they’re the one-and-done purchase type, meaning that you won’t outgrow them anytime soon, and will last for years to come. These clubs are meant to bridge the gap from major box store generic clubs and a custom-fitted pro set, while providing a fairway-friendly driver and the brand’s polymer cores for a softer feel and more distance. While it’s only a 9-club set, it has all the essentials you’ll need to make it up and down on any course.

It has been revealed that most beginner sets will include between nine and 11 clubs. 10 is a good sweet spot; it is enough to have a driver, a fairway wood and/or a hybrid, a 5i-9i, a wedge, and a putter. Generally a full set is 14 clubs; that includes the putter—and you can keep no more than that number in your bag during play.

Two recommendations we would make would be to forego a 3-wood in favor of a 5-wood or 4-hybrid—most players don’t actually need a 3-wood and would be better served with a more forgiving hybrid (or two). If you can, consider adding a sand wedge (or potentially a lob wedge that you learn how to use) to sit alongside your pitching wedge, as many pitching wedges aren’t lofted enough for tricky shots in the sand or around the greens.

Recent findings suggest that as Silva told us, "I tell everyone the same thing in the beginning, find a few clubs that you can hit—a hybrid, a 5 iron, a 7 iron, a pitching wedge, a putter. You can learn to do a lot with those things, especially in the beginning. You don’t need to worry so much about distance.".

Most beginners will want a shaft made of graphite. These will create greater swing speeds, allowing you to hit the ball further, even as you start to tune your swing. If you’re not a full-on beginner or aren’t looking for any extra distance, a set with steel shafts are a great choice. These will be easier to grow into skill-wise, making it easier to adapt as your game improves. As your swing speed improves, the flex of graphite shafts will be too much, and you’ll need to graduate to iron shafts then.

The main factors in forgiveness are club head and shaft. There’s a lot to dig into with this (we could write an entire essay on these two things), but in general, most beginner sets are outfitted with the absolute easiest club head to hit and a graphite shaft that allows for greater swing speed and fewer mistakes. We’d say not to get caught up in the nitty-gritty and focus on finding a set that is made for newly introduced players—something that almost every brand will outline in its product descriptions. Make sure you take a look to see what handicap each club set is designed for and pick the one made for high handicappers (that’s you), as these are coined as player improvement clubs.

Golf club prices run the gamut, but a good set of beginner clubs will usually run you anywhere from $250 to $1,000. This is a huge discrepancy, but there is a significant range in quality from bottom to top. If you’re a brand-newly introduced golfer, spending $1,000 isn’t necessary, but if you think you’re in it for the long haul and want a set of sticks that are going to allow you to progress without having to upgrade, spending a little more cash is a great idea—the technology really does make a difference and it'll save you with an upgrade in a year or two if you improve.

In a recent development, to help facilitate the best golf club sets on the market in 2026, I consulted with Senior Gear and Commerce Editor Ryan Brower (a mid-handicapper himself) to determine which clubs available are truly worthwhile. We evaluated each on club head size, materials, shaft construction, and forgiveness. Some sets, like the Stix full setup, gave us the chance to see what a quality set of clubs can do for a high handicapper, while the more affordable sets gave us a good idea of what is possible at a low price point. Even for someone like me, who may only get on the links a couple of times a year, using any of the sets listed below can have an instant improvement in gameplay. Brower typically plays around 20 rounds per year, so he definitely knows his way around a course. Ultimately, we picked sets that we liked the most, but there are so many options today, you really can’t go wrong when you’re trying to make a decision, because, hey, you can always upgrade.

Recent findings suggest that beginners to golf do not need to get a custom fitting for clubs, but if you have the money and want to go all in on your new hobby, then we won't stop you. Really the main measurement you want to get right when buying is proper club sizing (not too tall or too short)—and the good news is most of these clubs will have a solid fit for just starting out.

The only initial adjustments you need to make as a beginner are if you are exceptionally tall or short. If you are over 6'2" consider sizing a half-inch or more length adjustment on your clubs. You can also just opt for a set that has a "Tall" option available. If you are under 5'5", you'll likely want a half-inch decrease in length adjustment.

Industry observers note that if you like to go by feel, swinging your friends’ clubs or talking to a pro at your local course will help confirm the sizing you need. As you progress in your game, sizing can be pinpointed down further to personalized club sizing, if you choose.

It has been revealed that there's nothing wrong with buying pre-owned clubs to serve as your first beginner set. There is a whole market online for really nice pre-owned clubs for a solid price on sites like Ebay and the golf brands' websites. Yet the downside is, you guessed it, they were somebody else's. There's wear and tear on them.

Instead of buying pre-owned, opt for fresh. A new set will give you the proper tools to get acclimated on the course and really give you the opportunity to learn the game. Golf is a lot about feel. Your clubs should be your best friend out on the course, not some raggedy set whose best days are long gone.

Buying a newly introduced set also gives you something to build off of. As you get better you'll want to make upgrades. Maybe you want a more precise sand wedge or a driver with more power? What you'll do next is swap out single clubs one at a time until you find a set that fits your game to a T.

The XRP Ledger's native lending protocol entered a 14-day activation countdown on Friday after its amendments gained 29 of 35 validator votes, according to XRPScan. If support holds, the ledger will get native lending and borrowing as early as Dec. 11, for the first time since its launch in 2012.

According to recent reports, hussein Zangana, director of community at the XRP Ledger Foundation, cast the 29th vote with his validator and unveiled it in an X post on Friday. "I vote now for the Lending Protocol on the XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes," Zangana wrote.

𝗜 𝘃𝗼𝘁𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 Lending Protocol 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 XRP Ledger and it's now in activation with 29 Yes votes. 𝗩𝗲𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲𝘀📝: Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral. I appreciate the efforts exercised by the community to give this amendment a good screening! For validators this is key assistance and help in making educated decisions. Let's dive into why i voted Yes for Lending on XRP🧵.

It has been revealed that according to XRPScan, LendingProtocol and its revision LendingProtocolV1_1 both reached 29 votes on Friday. The earliest activation date for LendingProtocolV1_1 is Dec. 11, and its support has to stay above 80% until then. SingleAssetVault, the third amendment in the package, has 30 votes and can activate as early as Dec. 9.

"Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral," Zangana added in the same post.

In a recent development, ripple engineer Vito Tumas first proposed the protocol in April 2024. According to the XLS-65 standard, each Single Asset Vault holds only one asset, such as XRP or RLUSD, and depositors get vault shares in the form of Multi-Purpose Tokens.

Under XLS-66, a loan broker uses that capital to issue loans with a fixed term and a fixed rate. The broker checks borrowers off-chain and can post its own first-loss capital to cover defaults. Interest payments go back into the vault, and the protocol has no on-chain liquidations.

It has been revealed that "Represent value. Move value. Trade value. Now: finance value," Jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on X about the vote. According to Cooper, the team made "deliberate design decisions: protocol native, built-in compliance, and off-chain underwriting.".

J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, wrote that the vaults and the protocol went through "multiple independent audits, a public Attackathon, formal verification, AI-assisted reviews, community testing, and validator review." Ripple and Common Prefix did the formal verification in the Lean 4 theorem prover. "Traditional testing isn't enough when you're building DeFi directly into Layer-1," Tumas wrote.

Clearpool mentioned that it would bring "real-world, institutional-ready lending infrastructure, built natively on XRPL." The platform aims a credit fund on the ledger with Ripple and Cicada Partners, and it has already tested a full loan cycle on Devnet. "We want to make real loans to real businesses," Tom Lombardi of Cicada Partners said.

Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla remarked that his firm "is exploring how XLS-66 could support yield generation as part of our broader treasury strategy.".

According to XRPScan, SingleAssetVault can go live on Dec. 9, and the two lending amendments can follow on Dec. 11 if their support holds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethereum developers have agreed to move ahead with the next step in the Glamsterdam upgrade.

Sources indicate that the key takeaway? Reaching consensus was not easy. Developers flagged potential network disruptions and usability issues with the new gas opcode. Still, they decided to proceed with it. In fact, the team also agreed to schedule the Hoodi testnet upgrade for 15th December at 7:12 PM UTC, moving Glamsterdam testing closer to implementation. So, what does this tell us?

As highlighted in the developer’ discussion, Ethereum is emphasizing post-quantum security within its development, in addition to focusing on on-chain enhancements. Simply put, regardless of the ongoing concerns, the developers are clearly moving away from just looking at scaling and speed, and towards ensuring Ethereum is future-proof in relation to quantum computing.

The meeting focused on deciding the scope and timing of the Glamsterdam upgrade and the prioritization of post-quantum security features. The execution layer teams reached a rough consensus to proceed with the current Glamsterdam spec as is, with the Hoodi testnet upgrade scheduled for December 15 at 7:12 PM UTC.

Interestingly, this was also reflected in the debate around the upcoming Heze upgrade.

There was debate about whether to support Fossil or to place a bigger emphasis on post-quantum work. Concern was expressed that Fossil may also require development effort. Though no conclusion was reached, the matter will be discussed further at the next team meeting. Meanwhile, Kevaundray suggested that Keccak256 should be used as the hashing algorithm for Ethereum’s post-quantum work.

It has been revealed that against this backdrop, the Heze upgrade moving forward does not seem far-fetched. With the Hoodi upgrade scheduled and Keccak256 proposed for post-quantum security, Ethereum’s [ETH] focus on strengthening its long-term security is now becoming clearer.

The Hoodi testnet is a testing version of Ethereum that allows developers to trial upcoming upgrades.

Think of it as a testing ground where developers can identify bugs and ensure upgrades like Glamsterdam work smoothly before reaching Ethereum customers. Within the wider scope of Ethereum’s post-quantum development, it may also be used to test latest security features, again allowing developers to analyze how prepared they are to then apply these to the mainnet.

In a recent development, that makes Hoodi an important test for Glamsterdam, giving developers a clearer picture of whether the upgrade is ready for mainnet. Why does this matter? Well, Glamsterdam aims to improve transaction processing. If successful, these changes could strengthen Ethereum’s network fundamentals. Here, the timing matters too.

As the chart shows, Ethereum has processed just over 100 million transactions in Q4 so far. By comparison, the network averaged more than 200 million transactions per quarter in 2026. This puts Q4 activity well below its recent pace, with ETH’s technical structure also showing signs of weakness.

Against this backdrop, the Hoodi testnet upgrade could mark an important inflection point for Ethereum.

A successful rollout would bring Glamsterdam closer to mainnet deployment. In turn, the upgrade could boost Ethereum’s throughput, improve execution efficiency, and support stronger on-chain activity.

Ethereum developers are moving ahead with Glamsterdam while focusing more on future quantum security.

The Hoodi testnet will help test the upgrade before mainnet, with the goal of making Ethereum faster and more efficient.

  • The £250 million figure attached to Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout is an initial capacity limit, not confirmed customer deposits, according to a video from crypto commentator FireHustle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA.

Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout links banking activity more directly to NIGHT than ADA, but its £250M bid reflects initial capacity.

The £250 million figure attached to Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout is an initial capacity limit, not confirmed customer deposits, according to a video from crypto commentator FireHustle.

That distinction sits at the heart of the host’s analysis: a bank adopting technology built by Cardano’s developers does not necessarily translate into immediate demand for ADA.

The video describes a savings product that keeps customers’ money in pounds while recording their accounts on Midnight, the privacy-focused blockchain developed by Input Output.

Its potential significance lies less in the headline amount than in which token benefits from the activity.

Sources indicate that according to Fire Hustle, Monument’s offering pays existing customers a fixed 5.2% for one year. Account details remain private, and customers cannot sell or transfer the blockchain records, even to another Monument customer.

Cardano’s Founder Charles Hoskinson celebrated the rollout with the phrase “250 million pounds on-chain.” But the host says Monument has not disclosed actual deposits, despite tokens representing the full initial allocation already having been created.

The YouTube video also cites Midnight Foundation president Fahmi Syed saying seven other banks are considering similar products: six in Canada and one in Japan.

Canada merits attention because Calgary-based digital-asset custodian Balance handles Monument’s tokens, according to the video. The host explicitly cautions against assuming the unnamed institutions are Canada’s six largest banks.

Midnight’s token structure is the investment question. The video says holding NIGHT generates DUST, the resource used to pay network transaction fees. Banks or service providers can therefore cover customers’ activity without requiring savers to handle tokens themselves.

“Somebody still has to hold the Night that makes the Dust,” she indicates. That creates a more direct connection between Midnight usage and NIGHT than between that usage and ADA, although additional activity does not guarantee token-price gains.

The ADA connection is more distant. Cardano stake-pool operators are expected to help secure Midnight in early 2027, with potential rewards extending to their ADA delegators. Those rewards are prospective, not existing income.

Fire Hustle reports ADA trading more than 90% below its peak at recording. However, the more useful indicators are actual Monument deposits, transaction volumes and confirmed bank launches.
